title: Mining Museum Hall in Tirol
name: Mining Museum Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The Bergbaumuseum in Hall in Tirol: a faithfully recreated salt mine gallery in a vaulted cellar in the historic town centre featuring a slide, tools, and minerals.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Bergbaumuseum Hall in Tirol is located in the heart of the protected medieval historic town centre of Hall in Tirol (Bezirk Innsbruck-Land) on Fürstengraben at an elevation of around 560 metres above sea level. Established within the deep, barrel-vaulted cellars of a historic town residence, the museum brings the nearly 800-year history of traditional salt mining in Halltal vividly to life. In the Middle Ages, the "white gold" extracted from the Karwendel mountains brought tremendous wealth to the town of Hall, turning it into Northern Tyrol's premier centre of commerce and river shipping.

Authentic Mining Gallery & Miners' Slide

The exhibition is designed as a walk-through, faithfully reconstructed mining gallery: stepping into the cellar immediately transports visitors into the mysterious underground realm of Hall's miners. Heavy timber props support the replica shaft ceiling, while subdued lighting and acoustic sound installations replicating dripping water and hammer blows create an authentic pit atmosphere. An absolute highlight for children and families is the traditional wooden miners' slide (Knappenrutsche), allowing visitors to whiz down into the lower gallery levels just as the miners once did. On display are original pit lamps, drilling and blasting tools, historic protective workwear, as well as brilliantly coloured salt rocks and minerals from the Karwendel range. Historical documents and display panels illustrate the painstaking brine-evaporation process used in the boiling pans of Saline Hall.

Visit & Getting There

Bergbaumuseum Hall is open during the summer months from May to October as part of regular guided tours (group tours available year-round upon advance booking with the Hall-Wattens Tourist Board). Admission fees (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (6 to 16 years) approx. €3.50, toddlers free. Holders of the regional Schatzkarte Hall-Wattens enjoy free admission! Arriving by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte); parking is available in the Untere Stadt underground car park or Altstadt underground car park. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn train to Hall in Tirol station, from where a pleasant five-minute stroll through the historic town leads directly to Fürstengraben.

Tips

A museum visit can be perfectly combined with a walk to Münze Hall (Hall Mint) and Burg Hasegg castle, located just a few minutes' walk away. Those who wish to experience the original open-air historic mining sites after visiting the museum can hike along the historic Knappensteig trail through wild and romantic Halltal up to the former salt mines.
